name: Spinal Cord Lipoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Spinal Cord Lipoma

criteria.description: Identification of a well-demarcated lipomatous mass within or adjacent to the spinal cord on MRI
Presence of progressive neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord compression or tethering
Histopathological confirmation of mature adipose tissue in biopsy or surgical specimen

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic MRI findings plus compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required if imaging and clinical presentation are definitive.

searchTerms: slow worsening of lower limb spasticity

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tethered cord syndrome with neurological deterioration
searchTerms: worsening neurological symptoms from tethered cord
progressive nerve problems due to spinal cord tethering
neurological decline with tethered spinal cord

common.symptomName: Sensory disturbances including numbness and paresthesia in lower extremities
Bladder dysfunction with urinary urgency or retention
Back pain localized to affected spinal segment

searchTerms: difficulty walking due to leg weakness

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as subcutaneous lipomas or skin dimples overlying the lesion
searchTerms: skin lumps or dimples over spine

imaging: MRI showing hyperintense mass on T1-weighted images consistent with fat
Fat suppression sequences confirming lipomatous nature
Possible spinal cord tethering or displacement
other: Histopathology demonstrating mature adipose tissue without atypia
Intraoperative findings of lipomatous tissue infiltrating or compressing spinal cord

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse epidural fat accumulation rather than discrete intramedullary mass
Often associated with steroid use or obesity
Presence of open or closed neural tube defects
Associated cutaneous markers and bony abnormalities
Different MRI signal characteristics and enhancement patterns

redFlags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Severe localized spinal pain with neurological signs
references: Tekkök IH, et al. Spinal cord lipomas: clinical features and surgical management. Neurosurgery Clinics of North America. 2003.
Choi JY, et al. MRI characteristics of spinal cord lipomas. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2001.
